title: Heatmap + AB preflight notes (sprint review prep)
content:
Goal: quick preflight for tomorrow's Optimize/Evals sync (30m). Focus = one suspected quality regression from last canary + sanity-check A/B buckets + decide go/no-go for threshold rollback.

Topline hypothesis:
- New prompt normalization in v2026-08-29 changed tokenization for a subset of prompts (mainly long, multi-turn instructions). This correlates with a ~3.8% drop in pass-rate on the ‘billing-forms’ prompt set in canary. Suspect: prefix trimming + new tokenizer config.

What I need to bring to the meeting (data + artifacts):
- Heatmap: per-prompt delta between baseline (v2026-08-20) and canary (v2026-08-29). Filter to prompts with >=50 evals. (see Confluence page)
- A/B summary table: N, pass-rate, 95% CI, p-value, win-rate by prompt cluster (billing, onboarding, codegen).
- Top 10 counterexamples where model output regressed (copy of before/after answers).
- CI on metric we care about: "acceptance_rate_v2" (what the product uses) and human-score proxy (RM-sim).
- Quick latency/cost delta for canary vs baseline (so PM can weigh perf tradeoffs).

Preflight checks (quick list to run now):
- [ ] Re-run heatmap extraction for latest logs (cut at 2026-09-02 04:00 UTC) — kenji assigned.
- [ ] Verify prompt normalization code SHA in canary (PR 487) matches the one used by the eval harness. (Maya)
- [ ] Recompute A/B p-values using stratified bootstrap (prompt cluster strata). (Sienna)
- [ ] Pull top 50 regression examples into a shared gist for triage. (auto)

Early signals to watch for in the meeting:
- If p < 0.01 and effect size > 2.5% absolute on acceptance_rate_v2 for a product-relevant prompt cluster -> strong candidate for rollback.
- If regressions concentrated on <5 prompts but severity high -> consider targeted prompt patch instead of rollback.
- If cost/latency improved materially (>6% tokens/sec) but quality drop small (<1%) -> product might accept it; need PM buy-in.

Discussion agenda (30m):
1) 5m: quick recap of the change (what changed in tokenizer/prefix trimming; link PR 487).
2) 10m: heatmap walk-through + top regressions (I will share screen).
3) 5m: A/B stats and significance summary.
4) 5m: risk analysis & mitigation options (rollback vs targeted prompt patches vs tweak tokenizer config).
5) 5m: action items + owners.

Notes to self / friction points to call out live:
- The eval harness tokenization may not mirror prod perfectly — confirm with infra whether we used the same model binary. If not, put a big question mark next to all results.
- Human labels for the billing prompts are sparse; RM-sim is noisy here. We should avoid overinterpreting small deltas.
- There is a known flaky eval job (job-id: 2026-08-30-heatmap-07) that dropped ~12% samples; exclude it.

Initial triage results (quick summary I computed):
- Billing cluster: baseline pass-rate 84.2% -> canary 80.4% (∆ = -3.8%, p≈0.004 stratified bootstrap). N=1,240.
- Onboarding cluster: baseline 90.3% -> canary 90.1% (∆ = -0.2%, p≈0.33). N=2,100.
- Codegen cluster: small improvements (∆ +0.9%, p≈0.06) but concentrated on short prompts. N=820.

Proposed immediate next steps (if consensus to act):
- Option A (rollback): revert tokenizer change in canary and promote baseline (fast, global). Owner: Kenji. Target: 24-48h.
- Option B (targeted prompt patch): add a small normalization exception for billing prompts (detect long-instruction pattern and preserve spacing). Owner: Maya + PR 512. Target: 72h.
- Option C (monitor): keep canary, expand A/B sample, add manual review of top regressions (if effect not robust). Owner: Sienna. Target: +1 week.

Follow-ups to schedule after meeting:
- [ ] If rollback chosen, run full smoke suite and sanity evals before promote. (SRE + Eng)
- [ ] If patch chosen, create a 10-prompt promptset for prod smoke to ensure fix. (Maya)
- [ ] Update the Optimize dashboard with an annotation for v2026-08-29 change (so future drift alerts reference it). (Sienna)

Questions I want the group to answer live:
- Are there downstream customers exposed to billing prompts (PM check)?
- Is the RM-sim proxy acceptable as a primary signal for these prompts? (research/ops)
- Do we have capacity to run a rollback within 24h if we choose to? (SRE)

Random scratch/thoughts (notes-to-self):
- If targeted patch works, also consider adding a regression test into preflight to detect tokenization-dependent regressions (small prompt fuzzing).
- Might be worth a postmortem doc if rollback occurs (short timeline + impact).

Quick links / artifacts to open during meeting:
- Confluence: heatmap-analysis (linked above)
